question: Does indexing RCW 59.18.230's ten enumerated prohibitions separately make the section retrievable, and what does it cost?
verdict: retrieval fixed, product regressed — NOT shipped. Re-gated 2026-08-05: the gold set and a new labelled set both cleared it, then the 40-lease silver set reproduced the original false red. See silver_regate_2026_08_05.

gold_scan_shipped_published.note: already measured and published; not re-run, per the no-reruns-for-prettier-numbers rule

the_false_red.clause: 2. RENT. Rent is $2,450 per month, due on the first. Payments may be made by check, money order, or electronic transfer through the resident portal.
the_false_red.retrieved: RCW 59.18.230(2)(j) — 'Agrees to make rent payments through electronic means only'
the_false_red.why_it_is_false: The clause PERMITS three payment methods, two of them non-electronic. It is the opposite of an electronic-only mandate. Reproduced twice: green under the shipped index (where (2)(j) never arrives), red under the split.
the_false_red.mechanism: Making the governing prohibition reachable put a crisp, narrow rule in front of the judge, which then over-applied it to a permissive clause on the same topic. A retrieval fix surfaced a generation weakness that the missing document had been masking.

conclusion: The split is the only one of three candidates that moved the strict retrieval metric: hybrid .656, section completion .492 (unchanged), enumerated split .984.
It bought nothing on the gold set's outcome metrics, which were already perfect: 18/18 red and 18/18 citations under the shipped index.
It cost the cleanest published claim in the project — 0 false reds became 1, precision 1.000 -> .947.
So the strict metric is a LEADING INDICATOR, not an outcome. It correctly found a real retrieval gap; closing that gap made the product worse. Outcome metrics win.
Kept implemented and measured, enabled nowhere, same disposition as hybrid retrieval and section completion.

revisited_2026_08_05.why: The roadmap said shipping this needed a labelled permissive-vs-mandatory set rather than a prompt rule written against the single observed false red. That set now exists (evaluation/permissive_pairs.jsonl, 32 clauses across all ten prohibitions) and it said the opposite of what was expected, so the paid gold gate was re-run.
revisited_2026_08_05.what_changed_underneath: Nothing in the clause judge: `judge_clause` and `make_judge_prompt` are unchanged since bb0243e apart from a ScanMeter->UsageMeter annotation, and retrieval.py's diff is metering plumbing. What did change is the index — `build_enumerated_collection.py` gained `temperature=0` after this experiment (commit 210a9e0), the collection was rebuilt, and the RETRIEVAL metric was re-verified at .984 while the PAID PRECISION GATE was not re-run. So the published 'precision 1.000 -> .947' described an index that no longer exists. Provider-side drift on gpt-4.1-mini is the other candidate and cannot be excluded from outside; either way the gate result below is the current one.

permissive_labelled_set.reading: The split is better on both axes, not merely not-worse: it flags 10/10 prohibited clauses where the shipped index flags 8/10 (it reads the exculpation and arbitration-cost prohibitions as green with no citation at all), and it produces 0 false reds where the shipped index produces 2, both on (2)(h) and both citing RCW 59.18.340 instead.

the_false_red_did_not_reproduce.2026_07_29: red under the split, reproduced twice
the_false_red_did_not_reproduce.2026_08_05: not red under the split, in two labelled-set runs and the gold gate

conclusion: The gold gate passes under the split: 18/18 red, 18/18 citations, 0 false reds, 6/6 protections — identical outcomes to the shipped index, plus strict scan retrieval .492 -> .984.

So the stated blocker is gone and the disposition is a decision rather than a constraint. Not flipped in this round: enabling it changes what the runtime store must contain and what the image ships, and the 40-lease silver set — where precision is a measured lower bound rather than 1.000 — has not been run against the split.

The transferable point is unchanged and now better evidenced: a leading indicator is not an outcome. What DID change is that the outcome it was traded against was measured on an index that had since been rebuilt, and nobody re-gated it.
revisited_2026_08_05.superseded_by: silver_regate_2026_08_05 — the conclusion below ('the stated blocker is gone') was written from the gold set and a 32-clause labelled set, and the 40-lease set then showed both were too small to contain the failing clause shape.

silver_regate_2026_08_05.why: The gold set is 6 leases and the labelled set was 32 clauses. Neither is the widest net available; the 40-lease generated set is, and it had never seen the split.
reading: Recall went UP, to perfect: 61/61 against the shipped index's 60/61. The split catches the one planted violation the shipped index misses.
Citation accuracy and protections held exactly: 1.000 and 39/40.
False reds went 7 -> 10, precision .8955 -> .8592. Five are new, two of the baseline's seven disappeared.

audit_of_the_five_new_false_reds.text: by check or electronic payment to Landlord at the address provided
audit_of_the_five_new_false_reds.evidence: The judge's own explanation says the clause 'requires rent payment by check or electronic payment ONLY'. The word 'only' is not in the clause. It is the July failure, verbatim in mechanism.

audit_of_the_five_new_false_reds.text: Rent should be paid by check or electronic transfer to the Landlord's designated account
audit_of_the_five_new_false_reds.judged: REAL FALSE RED, and on the COMPLIANT lease
audit_of_the_five_new_false_reds.evidence: Same hallucinated 'only'. A red flag on the false-positive probe is the most expensive error this scanner can make.

audit_of_the_five_new_false_reds.text: If rent is not received by the fifth of the month, a late fee of $50 will be charged for each week
audit_of_the_five_new_false_reds.judged: GENUINE VIOLATION, unlabelled by the generator
audit_of_the_five_new_false_reds.evidence: (2)(i) protects rent paid within five days FOLLOWING the due date. Rent due the 1st is protected through the 6th; a fee triggered by non-receipt on the 5th charges inside that window. Same class as the six-of-seven unlabelled reds the baseline's hand audit already found.

audit_of_the_five_new_false_reds.text: Rent not received by the fifth (5th) day of the month will be subject to a $50 late fee
deposit is held in a trust account at First Sound Bank ... Interest earned, if any, accrues to the Tenant per local law
audit_of_the_five_new_false_reds.verdict: red in the run; YELLOW when re-judged
audit_of_the_five_new_false_reds.evidence: Re-judging returned yellow citing RCW 59.18.270 and .260, on the substantive ground that the statute gives deposit interest to the landlord absent a written agreement. A defensible caution, and unstable between runs.

labelled_set_updated.what_was_added: The three verbatim payment clauses above, as permissive_hard. The first version of the set missed this shape: its permissive (2)(j) clauses listed three or four methods, which reads as an open menu, while the silver set's bare two-item lists read as closed ones.
labelled_set_updated.result: The set now reproduces the failure: 3 false reds under the split, all on the terse two-method clauses, all citing (2)(j). A future attempt at this fix is now testable for $0.028 instead of $0.6.

decision: NOT SHIPPED. The July rejection stands, and the reason it looked overturned is that the two sets consulted first were too small to hold the failing clause shape.

Both indexes carry a real defect, in opposite directions. The shipped index reads the exculpation (2)(f) and arbitration-cost (2)(h) prohibitions as green with no citation at all — 8/10 on the labelled set — which is a silent false NEGATIVE. The split hallucinates the word 'only' into terse permissive payment clauses, including on the compliant lease, which is a false POSITIVE. This project's stated position is that a false red is the expensive error, so the shipped index keeps the default.

What changed that is worth keeping: the failure is now encoded in a labelled set rather than in a single anecdote from a paid run, and the shipped index's own (2)(f)/(2)(h) blind spot is now measured rather than unknown.
The honest next step is neither index but the judge: it is inventing exclusivity that the text does not contain. That is a generation fix, testable against permissive_pairs.jsonl for cents.
